findings.title: CORS policy reflects any Origin with credentials
findings.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers decide which other websites may read this site's responses from a visitor's browser.
findings.why: The server copied an arbitrary, unrelated Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and also sent Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. A malicious site can therefore make requests as a logged-in visitor and read the responses.

evidence.request:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8443
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate
Connection: keep-alive
User-Agent: AegisScan/0.1.0 (authorized security testing; non-destructive)
Accept: */*
Origin: https://aegisscan-cors-probe.example
Cookie: <redacted>
evidence.response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Apache/2.4.49 (Unix) OpenSSL/1.1.1k PHP/7.4.3
X-Powered-By: PHP/7.4.3
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://aegisscan-cors-probe.example
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Vary: Origin
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=<redacted>; path=/
Set-Cookie: prefs=<redacted>; Path=/; SameSite=None
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 581
evidence.note: The server copied an arbitrary, unrelated Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and also sent Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. A malicious site can therefore make requests as a logged-in visitor and read the responses.

findings.remediation: Compare the Origin header against an exact allow-list of trusted origins and return Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for those. Never reflect the request Origin, never allow 'null', and send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials only where it is needed. Add Vary: Origin.

findings.title: Session cookie 'PHPSESSID' has weak flags: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite

findings.title: Cipher suites without forward secrecy accepted
findings.description: TLS protects the confidentiality and integrity of everything sent to and from the site, and the certificate is what proves the server's identity.
findings.why: The server completed a handshake using static RSA key exchange, which has no forward secrecy: anyone who records traffic now and obtains the server key later can decrypt it. Negotiated: AES256-GCM-SHA384 over TLSv1.2.

findings.remediation: Allow only ECDHE (or DHE) key exchange, for example the Mozilla 'intermediate' configuration.
